requirements.evidence: Migration matches spec incl. unique (entity_id,email) and cascade (create_entity_invites_table.php:16-24); model normalizes e-mail via Attribute setter (EntityInvite.php:39-44); TTL 7 days + pending scope (EntityInvite.php:19,71-74); sendInvite validates 'required|email:strict|max:255' and admin/employee, rejects members and pending invites, replaces expired ones, converts unique violations into an inviteEmail error, queues mail, audits, resets, and rate limits only successful invites (Members.php:50-133); cancelInvite/openMember/saveRole/confirmRemoval/cancelRemoval/removeMember as specified (Members.php:135-234); PendingInvites accept/decline with idempotency, expiry error on 'invite', firstOrCreate, session + redirect (PendingInvites.php:23-83); onboarding/switcher embed with <hr> only when invites exist (pending-invites.blade.php:4-7, create-entity.blade.php:17); mail + translations present. Deviation: PendingInvites hides invites and returns 403 for users with unverified e-mails (PendingInvites.php:89-91,100-102), which the task does not ask for and may block 'registers then accepts' flows.

conventions.evidence: Docs and CHANGELOG updated (CHANGELOG.md:22, docs/business-rules.md:66, docs/database-schema.md), $fillable set via #[Fillable] (EntityInvite.php:11), policies used for authorization ($this->authorize('update', ...)). However the Livewire components drop the project's #[Validate] pattern in favour of inline $this->validate([...]) arrays (Members.php:55-58, 173-175; the Validate import is removed), domain writes (invite creation, acceptance/membership creation) are done inline in components instead of app/Actions/* use-case classes (Members.php:91-101, PendingInvites.php:41-57), and the migration name 2026_10_29_000001 does not look generator-produced.

security.evidence: Every mutating action authorizes server-side: sendInvite/cancelInvite/openMember/confirmRemoval authorize 'update' (Members.php:50,137,148,204), saveRole re-resolves the membership within the entity and authorizes 'assignRole' (Members.php:165-167, 246-251), invite IDs are scoped via $this->entity->invites()->findOrFail (Members.php:139); PendingInvites checks e-mail ownership before accept/decline (PendingInvites.php:28,74,106-108); owner role never invitable and owner fallback on accept; all output uses {{ }}; rate limit in place. Minor gap: selectedMembershipId/memberRole are plain client-writable properties (not #[Locked]); impact is limited because saveRole re-scopes and re-authorizes, but the Livewire policy prefers locking server context.

tests.evidence: InvitesTest.php covers normalization, uniqueness, factory/expired state, cascade, case-insensitive listing, accept happy path, idempotency, expiry error, no duplicate membership, stranger 403 on accept/decline, onboarding <hr> placement and both locales, switcher, mail rendering in en/pt_BR. MembersTest.php covers employee 403 (component + route), invite happy path, validation incl. owner tamper, member/pending/expired cases, error rendered once, simulated unique race, rate limit not consumed by invalid input, unauthorized send/cancel after role change, foreign invite/membership tamper, draft role, saveRole owner/last-manager rules, removal confirmation modal. Missing: unauthorized-call tests for openMember/saveRole/confirmRemoval/removeMember by a demoted user and a tamper test setting selectedMembershipId to a foreign membership before saveRole.

simplicity.evidence: Extracts managerCount() to remove duplication (Members.php:253-258) and reuses existing policies. Small excess: string-matching isUniqueViolation (Members.php:260-266) where Laravel's UniqueConstraintViolationException could be caught; unreachable owner->employee fallback in accept (PendingInvites.php:49) since owner is never invitable; duplicate lang key invites_pending_title vs invites_title (lang/en/ui.php); unused inviter() relation (EntityInvite.php:51-54).

readability.evidence: Clear method names and short comments explaining invariants ('Only an expired (or already consumed) invite may be replaced.', 'Idempotent: a double click...'); sendInvite is long (~80 lines, Members.php:48-133) mixing validation, duplicate checks, throttling, persistence and mailing; public methods lack PHPDoc. Blade views are consistent Bulma markup with wire:key.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task; navbar/dashboard edits hiding the members link from employees (default-page.blade.php:44-45, dashboard.blade.php, Dashboard.php:26) follow from the manager-only requirement. Unrequested extras: self-removal redirect/session reset (Members.php:229-233), verified-e-mail gating on invites, closeMember method.

issues.explanation: Invites are hidden and accept/decline return 403 for users whose e-mail is not verified, a restriction not in the task that can prevent a freshly registered invitee from seeing or accepting the invite.
Validation uses inline $this->validate([...]) arrays instead of the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern on public properties (inviteEmail, inviteRole, memberRole).
Domain writes (creating invites, accepting them into memberships) live inside Livewire components rather than in app/Actions/* use-case classes as the conventions require.
selectedMembershipId is server context but not #[Locked]; it is re-scoped in saveRole so impact is limited, but the Livewire policy asks for locking and no tamper test covers it.
No unauthorized-call tests for openMember, saveRole or confirmRemoval by a non-manager, and no tamper test for a forged selectedMembershipId.
Unique-violation detection by substring matching the exception message is fragile; catching Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException is simpler and exact.
invites_pending_title duplicates invites_title; the unused inviter() relation and unreachable owner fallback in accept add dead code.
The timestamp suffix 000001 suggests a hand-named migration rather than one created via php artisan make:migration.

review.summary: The change replaces direct member addition with a complete invite flow (table, model, factory, queued mail, PendingInvites component on switcher and onboarding) and turns the members page into a manager-only page with a detail modal, explicit save role and a removal confirmation modal, backed by thorough Pest tests and doc/changelog updates. Authorization and validation are solid; the main deviations are skipping the project's #[Validate] and Actions conventions, an unrequested verified-e-mail gate on accepting invites, and a few missing unauthorized/tamper tests, so it is approvable with minor follow-ups.
